report.source_text: The MRI of the thoracic spine with IV contrast revealed widespread osseous metastatic neoplasm, with significant involvement in the mid-thoracic spine, centered around T7. This region shows an enhancing mass extending into the posterior mediastinum and prevertebral soft tissues, potentially contiguous with the esophagus, suggesting a primary neoplasm. Additionally, there is a pathologic fracture of the T7 vertebral body with erosion into the anterior epidural space, causing spinal canal narrowing. Dural thickening is observed cranially and caudally from this region along the thoracic spine over a 12 cm span, roughly from T4 to T9 (Figures 1-2).

report.source_text: Congo red staining yielded negative results for amyloid deposition, and fungal stains also returned negative. Flow cytometry analysis demonstrated aberrancies in monocytes, specifically concerning CD2 and CD56 expression.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Stage II multiple myeloma with kappa light chain restriction and biopsy-proven bone plasmacytoma
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old man presented with progressive bilateral lower extremity weakness, numbness, and mid-lower back pain impairing ambulation. MRI of the thoracic spine revealed a destructive osseous metastatic lesion centered on T7 with epidural space involvement causing spinal canal narrowing. Biopsy of the T7 vertebral lesion confirmed a monoclonal kappa light chain-restricted plasmacytoma. Bone marrow biopsy showed approximately 12% monoclonal kappa plasma cell infiltrates consistent with plasma cell neoplasm. Congo red and fungal stains were negative. Flow cytometry noted monocyte aberrancies but did not contradict the plasmacytoma diagnosis. While serum protein electrophoresis and free light chain assays were either not reported or had unavailable results, the combined clinical, imaging, histopathologic, and bone marrow findings support the diagnosis of stage II multiple myeloma with kappa light chain restriction.
